rv.q: She is one of the best Juliets I have seen.
Happy are they who have a ticket already for this curious but nearly sold-out requiem.
It doesn’t always fully cohere, and it sometimes loosens its grip on our imagination; but Lloyd’s production is an arresting vision of an inequitable society in freefall...
Francesca Amewudah-Rivers is a radiant Juliet with a luminous stage presence whose performance single-handedly elevates the entire show...

Romeo & Juliet is a fascinating interpretation of the Shakespearean classic that, with the direction of Lloyd, allows the audience to see a sharp contrast between the darkness and light surrounding Verona.
There is an undeniable, captivating intensity to his smoky staging of Shakespeare’s tragic love story.
Although the production has a heartbeat, it's missing a heart.
Despite the unusual direction of scenes, the acting from the cast is superb, Tomiwa Edun’s Capulet is vicious, and Agyeman provides much needed comic relief in her portrayal of the nurse.
But what could make for an interesting thesis paper, or university lecture, hasn't translated into an equally interesting show.
Unfortunately, though, it's a depressingly lifeless affair, which somehow manages to be both overstated and underpowered.
As Romeo, Tom Holland is a charisma free zone, achieving the unlikely feat of being both buff and weedy.

cn.t: Lloyd's stark, gimmicky production of Shakespeare's tragedy divides critics, with Holland and Amewudah-Rivers' performances praised but the oppressively dark staging and stripped-back approach criticized for lacking emotional depth and heart.

vr.q: it was a big swing and a miss
